How to play & keyboard shortcuts

Select an axis below the 3D view, or select a ring, node, or axis label. Both panels share the selected axis. Grab and drag a ring to turn it. In 3D, Rotate ↶ is positive (counterclockwise) and Rotate ↷ is negative (clockwise), looking inward from the selected axis’s outer end. During a move, the axis button and applied rotation button light up together. Inner cube slices follow their named face; M follows L, E follows D, and S follows F. Drag the 3D puzzle to orbit; scroll or pinch to zoom.

Use ← and → for the selected ring. Keys A through L turn the matching face; hold Shift for the inverse. Face names A–L are local to this game. A prime (′) means counterclockwise viewed from outside that face; 2 means two 72° steps. The arrow buttons follow the ring’s on-screen direction, which can differ from a face’s notation.

Use the top playback-rate selector for ½× through 2× animation. During Auto Solve, Stop requests the end of the current sequence; click Stop now to finish only the current turn. Manual constrained Stop finishes only the current turn. A partial sequence may not yet restore held colors. Randomize and journal replay stop at the last completed turn.

Open the illustrated How to play for annotated ring-map and 3D examples, held colors, selection, playback, labels, and goal preview. The puzzle’s Solution guide explains its specific solving method.
